newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican union leader demands emergency wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Mexican union leader demands emergency wage hike.

text.p: The head of Mexico's most powerful labour union has threatened to organise demonstrations if the government fails to grant an emergency wage hike in the next few weeks.
"We'll take to the streets and if necessary we'll use our right to strike," said Leonardo Rodriguez Alcaine, head of the 6-million-strong Mexican Workers Confederation (CTM).
His comments were carried on the front page of La Jornada newspaper on Tuesday and were obtained by Reuters.

In an unusually belligerent message from the normally pro-government CTM, Rodriguez Alcaine said he would demand the hike from the Labour Ministry in the next 15 days, and he warned of possible violence if it were not accepted.
He noted that for years Mexican wage hikes have fallen short of price increases, partly because retailers pushed up their prices as soon as there was talk of a change in the minimum wage.
"The problem is...in this case, businesses have not complied and we don't want to expose either workers or businesses to a mess of this kind. We don't want violence," he said.
During Mexico's 1994-5 peso crisis, in which the economy suffered its worst recession in 50 years, Mexican workers saw their pay packets wither.
During the crisis, the CTM leadership clamped a lid on labour protests to avoid chaos for President Ernesto Zedillo as he applied drastic austerity measures.
